content: Mineral spirits, also known as Stoddard solvent, are a type of petroleum distillate frequently utilized as a paint thinner and a mild solvent. In Europe, this substance is commonly referred to as white spirit. Within industrial settings, mineral spirits are employed for cleaning and degreasing machine tools and mechanical parts. According to Wesco, a supplier of solvents and cleaning equipment, mineral spirits are particularly effective in removing oils, greases, carbon deposits, and other residues from metal surfaces. Mineral spirits can also be used in combination with cutting oil as a lubricant for thread cutting and reaming processes. Artists often use mineral spirits as a substitute for turpentine, as it is less flammable and less toxic. However, due to interactions with pigments, artists require a higher grade of mineral spirits compared to industrial users. This higher grade must be free of residual sulfur to meet the specific needs of artistic applications. Odorless mineral spirits are a refined version of mineral spirits, in which the more toxic aromatic compounds have been removed. These are recommended for applications such as oil painting, where humans are in close contact with the solvent. In the European Community, the composition of mineral spirits is regulated under Article 11(2) of Directive 2002/96/EC (WEEE).
